name: eyeWalker
display_name: eyeWalker — Real-time Navigation for Visually Impaired
description: Real-time world vision for visually impaired using Muse Spark 1.1 VLM. Detects obstacles (benches, pier edges, people, low branches) and guides via spatial audio: 'trash bin 2.1m ahead, step left 0.5m'. From NeuroAgent AI for rare neurologic diseases affecting vision.
author: NeuroAgent AI

rgb_frame.description: Real-time RGB frame from Ray-Ban or smartphone camera

user_speed_mps.description: User walking speed in m/s (e.g., 1.3 for 20'07 pace)

obstacles.description: Detected obstacles with [class, distance_m, direction_degrees, urgency, description]

guidance_audio.description: Spatial audio guidance: 'Trash bin 2.1m ahead, center. Step left 0.5m.'

risk_level.description: Overall scene risk based on obstacle urgency + user speed

output.guidance_audio: Trash bin 2.1 meters ahead, center. Step left half meter, then straight.

perception_pipeline: Depth Anything V2 for dense depth estimation
Muse Spark 1.1 VLM for open-vocab obstacle detection
SAM (Segment Anything) for walkable vs. non-walkable segmentation
architecture.fusion: GPS coarse + VIO fine + OSM ground truth snap for accurate localization
obstacle_taxonomy: static_ground: benches, trash cans, bollards, cones
ground_hazard: uneven pavement, curbs, puddles, pier drops
architecture.avoidance: Real-time path planner: compute bypass direction + distance + time-to-collision
architecture.output_modality: Binaural spatial audio rendered at 3D obstacle position

ground_truth_layer.map_source: OpenStreetMap (Overpass API) with custom filter for footway, path, pier, marina
ground_truth_layer.satellite: Esri World Imagery (<3yr freshness, free tier) for structural reference

safety: This is assistive, not replacement for cane/guide dog. Always keep traditional mobility aid. This is alpha. It is a research prototype for users and developers to improve upon.
use_cases: Real-time navigation on unfamiliar routes (harbor walks, city streets, piers, boardwalks)
Obstacle avoidance for blind/low-vision users walking with smartphone or Ray-Bans
Research baseline for accessible navigation systems
City-scale deployment (extend beyond Baltimore harbor to any OSM coverage area)

performance.accuracy: Tuned for 20'07"/mi walking pace (~1.3 m/s); TTC reaction window 0.8 sec
performance.device: Ray-Ban Meta or smartphone (iOS/Android via Expo React Native)

impact.global_burden: WHO: 2.2B people with vision impairment; 1B preventable; 2/3 without glasses in low-income countries; $411B annual productivity loss
impact.target_patients: NMOSD, MOGAD, optic neuritis, LHON, OPA1, Wolfram, IIH, CVI + all glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, AMD, RP, hemianopia, TBI
impact.origin: Inspired by daily post-lunch harbor walks — 3.66mi loop around Baltimore's Fells Point, Frederick Douglass-Isaac Myers Maritime Park, Harbor Point, marinas where standard maps fail
